a:r.a:t: Degradation of Amino Acids to Pyruvate

p:cNvPr.descr: An outline of the catabolic pathways for alanine, glycine, serine, cysteine, tryptophan, and threonine. It begins with threonine in a box where CH bonds right to COO- (C is in blue), up to NH3 (plus sign on N), and left to CH (C in pink box). CH bonds left to CH3 (C in pink box) and bonds down to OH. Below this is an arrow pointing down to 2-amino-3-ketobutyrate, identified as threonine dehydrogenase (in blue). To the right is a curved arrow from NAD+ to NADH. 2-amino-3-ketobutyrate beings with C (in pink box), double bonds down to O, bonds left to CH3 (C is in pink box), and right to CH. CH bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N), and right to COO- (C is blue). This has an arrow pointing down, identified as 2-amino-3-ketobutyrate CoA ligase (in blue). On the right is a curved arrow pointing from CoA to Acetyl-CoA (in a pink box). Below this is glycine in a box, where NH3 (plus sign over N), which bonds down to CH2, which bonds right to COO- (C is in blue). An arrow points right from the glycine box to CO2 (C is in blue) [plus] NH4+. This arrow is identified as glycine cleavage enzyme. Above the arrow is a curve arrow pointing from NAD+ to NADH. Below the glycine molecule are reversible lines, identified as serine hydroxymethyltransferase (in blue). To the right is a curved arrow pointing from H2O to H4 folate, with PLP in the middle of the arc. Another beginning with N5, N10-methylene (in pink) and H4 folate merges with the curved arrow and points to H4 folate. An arrow from H4 folate points right, then up and around glycine cleavage enzyme (in blue), and points to methylene (in pink). Below this is serine in a box, which begins with HO, which bonds right to CH2 (C is in pink), which bonds right to CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N), which bonds right to COO- (C is in blue). Below this is an arrow pointing down to pyruvate in a blue box. This arrow is identified as serine dehydratase (in blue). To the right is an arrow identified as PLP pointing right to H2O. Below that is another curved arrow pointing from H2O to NH4+. Pyruvate begins with CH, which double bonds up to O, bonds left to CH3 (C is in pink) and right to COO- (C is in blue). To the right of this is an arrow pointing to pyruvate from cysteine in a box, with “2 steps” written on top. This begins with CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N), right to COO- (C is in blue), and left to CH2 (C is in pink), which bonds up to SH. To the left of pyruvate is an arrow pointing to pyruvate from alanine in a box, identified as alanine aminotransferase (in blue). Below this arrow is a curved arrow pointing from alpha-ketoglutarate to glutamate. PLP is in the middle of the arc. Alanine begins with CH, which bonds left to CH3 (C is in pink), right to COO- (C is in blue), and up to NH3 (plus sign over N). Tryptophan in a box is above this and has an arrow pointing down to alanine, with 4 steps. Tryptophan begins with CH, which bonds right to COO- (C is in blue), up to NH3 (plus sign over N), and left to CH2 (C is in pink). This bonds down and left to a pentagon with a hexagon to the left. The bottom right point is N over H. The top right has double-bonded side. The pentagon shares its left side with the right side of a hexagon. This shared side is double-bonded. The hexagon has alternating double signs.
